answer: Beacon-Linked Task Assignment. Each agent gets work only when its periodic beacon (a signed uptime proof) is anchored to a randomly assigned opal—a unique, verifiable artifact minted per identity and checked by peers. New identities must independently complete a costly blind calibration task before receiving any beacon, and the opal rotates on each assignment. Cloning N agents means N separate calibrations plus N simultaneous beacon proofs; any missed anchor voids that identity's opal, forfeiting all accumulated task credit. Marginal clone cost stays strictly above expected payout.
